_about: Customer words for every message the server sends to a screen (UI standard, product owner 2026-10-16): a short label for the main screen and a structured detail — what it means, why, what to do next — for its pop-up. Read by core/messages.py; values fill {placeholders}.

detail.what: The request could not be completed.
detail.next: Try again. If it keeps happening, raise a request in Support and say when it happened.

detail.what: What you asked for does not exist, or your organisation cannot see it.
Your role does not include this action.
detail.next: Ask an administrator in your organisation.

detail.what: {what}
The asset has no coordinates, so no hazard can be read at it.
detail.next: Add the asset's latitude and longitude in Your data.

detail.what: The {map} have not been read at this location yet.
detail.next: Run losses again — a run reads any new location first.

detail.what: The location lies outside the area the {map} cover.
Your organisation has not chosen the damage curves for {peril} losses.
detail.next: Choose them in Settings → Methodology.

detail.what: The damage curves chosen for {peril} do not yet match the hazard data the platform holds.
detail.next: Choose another family of curves in Settings → Methodology, or wait for the platform to support these.

detail.what: The building's use (residential, commercial or industrial) is not stated, and the asset type '{type}' does not settle it.
detail.next: State the building use in Your data.

detail.what: Neither the building's use nor the asset's type is stated.
detail.next: State the building use in Your data.

detail.what: The asset's country is not stated, and damage curves are chosen by country.{hint}
detail.next: State the country in Your data.

loss.gap.country_group.label: Country is a group, not a country

detail.what: Your data states '{stated}', a group of countries; damage curves are chosen by country.{hint}
detail.next: State the asset's own country in Your data.

loss.gap.no_curve.label: No curve for this use and country

detail.what: The chosen damage curves include no {use} curve for {country}.
detail.why: The publisher did not publish one for this region.

detail.what: The building's own value (land excluded) is not stated.
detail.why: A damage curve gives a share of the building's value; a market or appraised value includes the land, so it is never used instead.
detail.next: Add the building value in Your data.

detail.what: A holding is a share in a company, not a building, so no building damage curve applies to it.
The site's building value is not stated; its annual value is a flow, not what the building is worth.
detail.next: Add the building value in Your data.

detail.what: The asset's value is not stated.
detail.next: Add it in Your data.

loss.gap.no_damage_range.label: No damage range at this depth

detail.what: The damage curve publishes no range at a depth of {depth} m.
No published projection of {peril} is available yet, so only today's figure exists.
The flood projections the platform uses were not run for {scenario}.
detail.why: The publisher ran two warming pathways only.

detail.what: The flood projections the platform uses publish no map for {year}; their last period, 2060–2099, is offered as 2080.
Local flood defences here are designed for the 1-in-{years}-year river flood. Losses from more frequent floods are set to zero.
detail.why: Source: the JRC map of estimated flood-protection standards in Europe.

detail.what: The flood-protection map has not been read at this location yet; the loss shown is undefended.
detail.next: Run losses again — a run reads any new location first.

detail.what: The flood-protection map holds no value at this location; the loss shown is undefended.
The location lies outside the flood-protection map (geographical Europe except Russia, Belarus, Ukraine and the Caucasus); the loss shown is undefended.
Defences are not applied to future climates yet.
detail.why: The projections' publisher moves protection levels with the climate, using its own protection data — a method not yet decided.

detail.what: The map's publisher flags this area: depths above 10 m in small channels may come from the model or the terrain data rather than a real flood.
detail.next: Use this figure with care.

detail.what: Your supervisor always sees your figures by region (NUTS-3), the level your filings report at. It sees the locations of individual sites only while you grant site-level access.
detail.why: Regional figures are what supervisory filings carry. Site locations are more sensitive, so opening them is your decision.
detail.next: Grant or revoke site-level access at any time. Each change is recorded in your audit trail and in your supervisor's.

detail.what: Your supervisor may share its case file on you with another authority, a supervisory college or a committee.
detail.why: Each share covers only the sections listed, carries a watermark, and stops working at its expiry or when your supervisor revokes it.
detail.next: Every share and every download also appears in your audit trail.

detail.what: Each requirement is checked against your regulatory attributes, using the criteria its act sets out.
detail.why: Where an attribute the criteria need is not stated, the result is 'Cannot determine', never a guess.
detail.next: State the missing attributes under Regulatory attributes on this page.

supervision.respondent.no_template.label: No template set up for your sector

detail.what: {regulator} has not set up a template for organisations in your sector yet.
detail.next: Answer its requests on this page instead.

detail.what: Your at-risk threshold is sent with the template: the hazard score (0 to 100) at or above which you treat an exposure as at material physical risk.
detail.why: Your supervisor reads your share of sensitive exposure at this threshold, on your own definition.

detail.what: Your at-risk threshold is the hazard score (0 to 100) at or above which you treat an exposure as at material physical risk.
detail.why: Without it, your supervisor cannot read your share of sensitive exposure on your own definition.
detail.next: Enter it with this submission, or state it in your organisation's methodology settings.

detail.what: This supervision was acknowledged before, or it is not one of your organisation's.

supervision.respondent.empty_reply.label: Write a message or choose a status

detail.what: A reply to your supervisor needs a message, a new status, or both.

supervision.respondent.status_not_allowe.label: This status is not yours to set

detail.what: Your side cannot move this {kind} from {from_status} to {to_status}.
detail.why: Your supervisor sets the other statuses, including closing the request.

supervision.respondent.attribute_not_you.label: This attribute is not set here

detail.what: {attribute} comes from your organisation's record, or is not a regulatory attribute.
{attribute}: enter a number for amounts and counts, and yes or no for the others.
Your role cannot submit a template to a supervisor.
detail.next: Ask an administrator in your organisation.

supervision.respondent.unreadable_file.label: The file could not be read

detail.what: Upload a CSV or Excel (.xlsx) file whose first row holds the column names.
Some required columns were not found, or some rows have problems.
detail.next: Check the file again to see which, correct them, and submit.

supervision.respondent.basis_invalid.label: The stated basis was not accepted

detail.what: The at-risk threshold must be a number from 0 to 100, and a stated scenario or horizon must be one of those offered.
detail.next: Correct the stated basis and submit again.

detail.what: The template could not be saved.
detail.next: Check the file and try again. If it keeps happening, raise a request in Support.

detail.what: Receipt of this letter was acknowledged before; it is recorded once.
This entity is not part of the population your authority supervises, so its intake cannot be opened.
detail.next: Open the entity from Population.

detail.what: Intake is set up per sector in your supervision profile, and this entity's sector is not in it.
detail.next: To supervise this sector, choose a profile that includes it in Settings. The entity's regional exposure and filings stay on its file.

detail.what: A file here is either the template the entity submitted or your own granular data.

supervision.intake.unreadable.label: The file could not be read

detail.what: The file is not a table this screen can read.
detail.next: Upload a CSV or Excel file with the column names in its first row.

detail.what: {n} required fields are not matched to a column of your file: {fields}. Nothing has been saved.
detail.next: Match each required field to a column, then check the file again.

supervision.intake.no_valid_rows.label: No complete rows in the file

detail.what: Every row has a problem, so there is nothing to save.
detail.next: Correct the flagged rows in your file and upload it again.

detail.what: '{period}' is not a financial year. Supervisory periods are financial years, such as FY2025.
{problem}
detail.next: Choose the scenario and year the entity states, and enter an at-risk level from 0 to 100, or leave them empty if it states none.

detail.what: Scenario projections run on the locations in your granular data, and none is on file for this entity yet.
{rows} rows were saved as {cells} template cells for {period}. Rows with problems are left out: {skipped}.
detail.next: Open the independent lens to compare it with the template rebuilt from your granular data.

detail.what: {rows} rows imported: {located} placed on the map, {unlocated} without a usable location. Rows with problems are left out: {skipped}. This import replaces your earlier granular data for this entity.
detail.next: Scores and scenario projections are computed in the background. The figures on this page update as they finish.

detail.what: Projections are running for {n} locations under every scenario and year. The figures on this page update as they finish.
This column must hold a number, such as 1250000 or 1.250.000,00.
detail.next: Correct the value in your file and upload it again.

detail.what: This column must hold a date written as year-month-day, such as 2031-06-30, or an Excel date cell.
detail.next: Correct the value in your file and upload it again.

detail.what: This field is required, and the row leaves it empty.
detail.next: Fill it in your file, or match the field to another column.

detail.what: Production, harvested area and yield by country and year, from 1961, for the crops and countries the platform covers — published by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO).
detail.why: FAO publishes about once a year and revises earlier years. The platform checks for a new file every month. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

detail.what: Area, production and yield by country and year in the EU, EFTA, the UK and candidate countries — including durum wheat, which FAO does not separate, and the latest season before FAO publishes it.
detail.why: The platform compares Eurostat's update date every month. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

detail.what: Area, production and yield by EU region (NUTS 2, 2021 version) and year, for the crops Eurostat publishes by region. Wheat is the sum of common and durum wheat. National figures come from Eurostat's national publication.
detail.why: The platform compares Eurostat's update date every month. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

detail.what: Official production, area and yield estimates by country and marketing year from the US Department of Agriculture's Foreign Agricultural Service — the current and recent seasons, ahead of FAO's one-to-two-year delay. Where USDA defines a crop differently from FAO (milled rice, palm and olive oil, shelled almonds), the platform's crop list says so.
detail.why: The platform compares USDA's release dates every month. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

reference.release.source.usda_nass.label: USDA crop production, US and states

detail.what: Production, area and yield for the United States and each state from the US Department of Agriculture's National Agricultural Statistics Service — annual survey estimates only.
detail.why: The platform asks every month for figures USDA has added since the last release. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

reference.release.source.usda_nass_count.label: USDA crop production by US county

detail.what: Production, area and yield for each US county on the Census Bureau's 2020 county list, published once a year after USDA's annual summary.
detail.why: The platform asks every month for figures USDA has added since the last release. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

detail.what: Area, production and yield for Canada and each province, including durum wheat — final production only.
detail.why: The platform compares the file's publication date every month. A new file waits on this page until it is reviewed and approved; nothing reaches customers' figures before that.

reference.release.reading_changed.label: Our reading of this source changed

detail.what: The rules the platform uses to read this publisher's file changed since its last applied release — for example, more countries, regions or crops are now read.
detail.why: Rows shown as added or recomputed can come from the new reading, not from the publisher changing its figures.
detail.next: Check that the added rows are the ones the new reading should bring before you propose the release.

detail.what: With one approver stated, the platform proposes each new release itself, with its counts as the review note, and one person approves it.
An operator reviewed this release of {source} and proposes applying it. Approving applies its figures to the platform's data; returning it closes the release and applies nothing.
The publisher gives the harvested area for the year but no production, so no yield can be read.
detail.why: This is usually the area of a season still in progress, or a production figure the publisher withholds.

detail.what: The publisher gives a symbol instead of a figure — for example (D), withheld to protect individual farms, or (NA), not available. The row is not read.
The publisher marks the value as not published — not available, confidential, or too unreliable to publish. The row is not read.
The publisher reports these states together. The figure belongs to no single state, so it is not read as one.
The publisher adds several provinces together. The figure belongs to no single province, so it is not read as one.
The publisher combines small counties into one figure to protect individual farms. It belongs to no single county, so it is not read as one.
The county is not on the Census Bureau's 2020 county list — it was renamed or dissolved since. The row is not read.
For a season still in progress, the publisher repeats its latest forecast as the year's figure.
detail.why: A forecast is not an estimate. The year is read once the publisher gives its estimate.

reference.release.aside.season_prelimina.label: Season in progress (before the final survey)

detail.what: Figures released before the November survey are model-based estimates, not final production.
detail.why: The year is read once the final figures are published.

detail.what: The regional publication also lists national and EU totals.
detail.why: National figures come from Eurostat's national publication, so they are not read twice.

detail.what: Regional figures are read at NUTS 2. Figures for the larger NUTS 1 regions are not read, so no area is counted twice.
Eurostat's extra-regio codes hold figures that belong to no region. They are not read.

reference.release.aside.other_nuts_versi.label: A region of another NUTS version

detail.what: The region code belongs to an earlier or later version of the EU's region list. Regions are read on the 2021 version only.

reference.release.aside.part_unpublished.label: A summed crop with a part missing

detail.what: Some crops are the sum of two published crops — wheat is common wheat plus durum wheat. Where one part is not published for the region and year, the sum would be wrong, so the row is not read.
Calibrations that read the crop's yield against drought in its growing season.
Calibrations that read the crop's yield against heat in its growing season.
Calibrations that read the crop's yield against soil-water stress in its growing season.
A new publisher file is applied to the platform's data only after this approval.
A new or re-run crop calibration is published only after this approval.
No release with this reference exists.
The platform has no reviewed data source with this name.
Rows are shown as added, revised or recomputed.
A release of {source} is still waiting for review or approval. A source has one open release at a time.
detail.next: Apply or reject the open release first.

reference.release.error.unknown_regions.label: Regions not on the region list

detail.what: The file names regions the platform's region list does not hold: {regions}. The file is refused and nothing is stored.
detail.next: Check the publisher's region codes against the official lists the platform reads.

reference.release.error.not_awaiting_rev.label: This release is no longer awaiting review

detail.what: It was proposed, applied or rejected since the page was loaded.
detail.next: Reload the page to see where it stands.

reference.release.error.not_awaiting_dec.label: This release is not awaiting a decision

detail.what: It was already decided, or it was never proposed.
detail.next: Reload the page to see where it stands.

detail.what: A note of at least 10 characters is needed. It is kept with the release.

reference.release.error.reject_note_requ.label: Say why the release is rejected

detail.what: A note of at least 10 characters is needed. It is kept with the release.
The platform has no approval rule with this name.
A change is approved by two people, or proposed by the platform and approved by one person.
A note of at least 10 characters is needed. It is kept in the audit record.
